{{Article header|deck=Surface deposit mining removes visible deposits from an asteroid with an abrasion blaster.}}

'''Surface deposit mining''' is the use of an [[Abrasion Blaster]] to break visible deposits from an asteroid. It often appears as the collection stage after [[Core Mining|core mining]], but the technique is distinct from normal laser mining because it targets named deposits rather than ordinary laser fragments.

{{Draft warning}}

== When to use surface deposit mining ==

Surface deposit mining is used when a deposit is visible and targetable on the asteroid surface. The most common teaching context is core mining: after a successful detonation, the cracked asteroid exposes deposits that must be broken free before collectors can recover them.

It can also appear as a targeted deposit task. In either case, the commander should treat the abrasion blaster as a precision extraction tool, not as a general mining laser.

== Equipment ==

A surface-deposit setup needs:

* [[Abrasion Blaster]] — dislodges the visible deposit.
* [[Collector Limpet Controller]] — retrieves the released material.
* [[Refinery]], cargo space, and limpets.
* [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] — helps identify asteroid contents.
* [[Pulse Wave Analyser]] — useful when searching for core-style targets that may expose deposits.

== Workflow summary ==

# Identify an asteroid with visible surface deposits.
# Target a deposit and fire the abrasion blaster to dislodge it.
# Let collector limpets retrieve the released resource.
# Refine the collected material into cargo where applicable.
# Ignore or vent unwanted refinery contents before they block useful fragments.

== Practical notes ==

* If a core asteroid has just been cracked, look for remaining exposed deposits before leaving.
* Deposits have to be targeted and struck cleanly; spraying the rock like a laser-mining asteroid is inefficient.
* The technique depends on collectors and refinery space just like the other mining methods.
